title: Twenty regional SST checks leave radiative trend error in five linear model kernels
abstract: We test what exact regional SST checks can rule out in five published atmosphere-model kernels at 60S-60N. An area RMS trend error of 0.01 K per decade can preserve 20 regional means and cause 0.0165-0.0372 W m-2 per decade of radiation-trend error. A linear program finds one pattern with every box error at most 0.02 K per decade and at least +0.02080 W m-2 per decade in every model. Restriction to 20 by 20 degree cells still permits +0.01291. At a fixed SST trend of 0.13 K per decade these common effects are at least 0.160 and 0.099 W m-2 K-1. Two kernel modes capture 90.8% of squared sensitivity, but two modes learned from four models leave 42-71% of the worst-case bound in the fifth. The bounds are sharp under the stated constraints. They show limits of regional validation; they do not show that such errors occurred. The package gives code, diagnostic weights, certificates and product-difference tests. Linear kernels, a fixed ice-free mask and chosen error budgets limit the result.

display.caption: Sharp conditional radiation bounds and tests of two diagnostic indices on a model left out of their construction.
A constructed trend error with area RMS 0.01 K per decade. It preserves all 20 regional means and has the same radiation sign in all five kernels.

citations.reason: Uses five symmetric box kernels and mask; extends specific artifact calculations to sharp validation bounds.
Uses published trend maps for the common mask and descriptive product-pair tests.
Related shared-error bound for acceleration; this study concerns spatial radiation sensitivity.
